section_summary: This section covers State Department, Army, and SCAP policies and actions regarding Japanese economic deconcentration and antitrust enforcement under Law No. 207 and the Anti-Monopoly Law between 1947 and 1949. It details internal government debates over the dilution of deconcentration measures by the Deconcentration Review Board, the impact of the Dodge economic stabilization program, and specific corporate reorganizations approved by the Holding Company Liquidation Commission. In addition, documents examine antitrust questions in Japanese shipping conferences and negotiations concerning potential American private participation and investment in the Japanese tobacco monopoly.

subfiles.about: Discussion between State Department official Fassberg and House Judiciary Committee Counsel Bernhardt regarding obtaining the Deconcentration Review Board report.
subfiles.summary: Bernhardt requested the Deconcentration Review Board report for the Celler Committee's monopoly investigation; Fassberg promised copies once received.
subfiles.title: Japanese Deconcentration

subfiles.about: Meeting discussing proposals to review the Japanese Fair Trade Commission and State Department communications with SCAP under NSC 13/2.
subfiles.summary: Thorp rejected dispatching two reviewers for the Fair Trade Commission, requesting a concrete proposal before approaching Acheson or Webb.
subfiles.title: Japanese Deconcentration

subfiles.about: Report warning that U.S. deconcentration policy is being weakened following Diet amendments and Walter Hutchinson's appointment by SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Martin warns that Diet antitrust amendments and Hutchinson's appointment weaken deconcentration, urging high-level review of the Deconcentration Review Board's minimizing actions.
subfiles.title: Significant Developments in Japanese Deconcentration Policy

subfiles.about: Analysis of how industrial rationalization under the Dodge economic stabilization program threatens to recreate prewar monopolies.
subfiles.summary: Martin stresses that Dodge Mission stabilization measures concentrating production necessitate maintaining strong antitrust laws to prevent prewar industrial reemergence.
subfiles.title: Pending Amendments of the Japanese Anti-trust Law and the Economic Stabilization Program
subfiles.to: Willard L. Thorp and Paul H. Nitze

subfiles.about: Call for high-level State Department action opposing Hutchinson's recommendations and Far Eastern Division's acquiescence in diluting Japanese deconcentration.
subfiles.summary: Dixon urges top-level intervention against curtailing deconcentration, arguing Hutchinson's reports and Army-FE policy undermine Japanese democratization and risk congressional scrutiny.
subfiles.title: Japanese Deconcentration

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Department of the Army suggestions and textual criticisms regarding proposed policy on Japanese economic deconcentration.
subfiles.summary: Gray transmits Army comments advising higher market-share thresholds, protection for patents and operating efficiency, and elimination of overly broad divestment language.
subfiles.title: Comments on Proposed 'Policy on Excessive Concentrations of Economic Power in Japan'

subfiles.about: Complaints concerning Northeast Asian Affairs Division using NSC 13/2 to block policy communications and information requests to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Vernon cites instances where NA blocked cables concerning antitrust amendments, General McCoy's deconcentration statement, and trademark policy under NSC 13/2.
subfiles.title: Use of NSC 13/2 to Prevent Necessary Communications Between the Department and SCAP

subfiles.about: Personal letter from SCAP Antitrust Chief Welsh discussing practical standards and obstacles facing Zaibatsu combine deconcentration.
subfiles.summary: Welsh defends SCAP's deconcentration standards, asserting that breaking up Zaibatsu operating combines improves management and lowers costs without impairing production.
subfiles.title: Deconcentration Problem in Japan and Holding Company Liquidation Commission Ordinance

subfiles.about: Critique of General Philip Fleming's letter to General MacArthur regarding antitrust standards and shipping conference practices in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Fassberg refutes General Fleming's arguments against applying antitrust standards to shipping conferences, highlighting discriminatory conference practices and exclusive arrangements.
subfiles.title: Japanese Shipping

subfiles.about: Official record replacement sheet noting substitution of unreturned action copy of Despatch 576 from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Official form designating a record copy to replace unreturned original action copy of Despatch 576 from Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Replacement Record Sheet for Despatch 576 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report detailing the status, final orders, and proposed orders for corporate reorganizations under Law No. 207.
subfiles.summary: This despatch presents a detailed review of the economic deconcentration program under Law No. 207, reporting that 297 of 325 designated companies were released without reorganization. It provides in-depth case studies of eleven companies receiving final orders and six receiving proposed orders, including major firms in steel, paper, beer, mining, and electrical manufacturing. The report concludes that the program has had limited overall effectiveness and notes unresolved issues regarding the electric power industry and large financial institutions.
subfiles.title: Survey of Economic Deconcentration Program in Japan

subfiles.about: State Department instruction acknowledging Despatch 576 and requesting further assessments of the antitrust program and post-treaty prospects.
subfiles.summary: Department praises the deconcentration survey and requests further reports on popular support and post-peace treaty prospects for antitrust enforcement.
subfiles.title: Department Request for Further Reports on Japanese Anti-Trust Program
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Draft queries to the Political Adviser regarding the effectiveness, public support, and continuation of antitrust reforms after the peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Draft airgram containing five specific queries evaluating whether Law 207 fulfilled occupation goals, public support, and post-treaty continuation measures.
subfiles.title: Draft Outgoing Airgram Concerning Japanese Deconcentration and Anti-Trust Policy

subfiles.about: Transmittal memorandum submitting the revised draft airgram to USPOLAD Tokyo for Northeast Asian Affairs Division concurrence.
subfiles.summary: Dixon forwards revised draft airgram incorporating NA's suggestions to solicit POLAD's evaluation of the deconcentration program and requests concurrence.
subfiles.title: Attached Airgram

subfiles.about: Detailed report on negotiations by American tobacco firms to participate in the Japanese tobacco monopoly and proposals for private management.
subfiles.summary: This despatch details discussions between American representative Emile Baruch of China-American Leaf Tobacco Company and Japanese officials regarding leaf supply and a proposed joint cigarette manufacturing venture. It reviews earlier overtures by British-American Tobacco Company and reports the cautious or skeptical reactions of SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section, Japanese farmers, and labor unions. Finally, it analyzes Premier Yoshida's controversial push to denationalize the tobacco monopoly despite strong opposition from the Ministry of Finance and leading press over vital state revenues.
subfiles.title: Discussions between China-American Leaf Tobacco and the Japan Monopoly Public Corporation

subfiles.about: Summary translation of a Japanese newspaper editorial urging extreme caution regarding Premier Yoshida's proposal to denationalize the tobacco monopoly.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo Shimbun editorial urges caution regarding tobacco denationalization, arguing vital state revenue must be protected and scarce foreign capital prioritized for essential industries.
subfiles.title: Consider Private Tobacco Business Cautiously (Tokyo Shimbun Editorial)
